sourceReasoning.reason: Omitting the optional third argument sets eligible to true, so the added guard is false. The old branches remain identical: null options yield unverified with the supplied previous value; a chosen match yields selected; a chosen miss yields ineligible; no choice yields unselected for a nonempty list and none for an empty list.
sourceReasoning.coverageLimit: The retained test explicitly exercises the two-argument null/empty/unselected cases and explicit true selection; full default compatibility follows from the unchanged branches and default value.

sourceReasoning.case: ineligible saved choice with discovered options
sourceReasoning.reason: For a supplied saved Agent IRI and eligible=false, line 75 returns ineligible before option lookup. A matching discovered option cannot restore selection; an empty list, a list without that IRI or a list with another Agent cannot substitute a selection. previous is the exact chosen input.

The chosen-and-ineligible guard precedes the null-options branch, so null options plus a saved choice and eligible=false yields ineligible with the original IRI, rather than downgrading known ineligibility to unverified. Without an explicit false eligibility, discovery failure retains the old unverified result.

readSession passes state.sessionAgent.actingSubject and state.sessionAgent.eligible directly. It does not pass mainAgent or initialActingSubject. The early return copies chosen into previous; the eligible branch selects only options.find(option => option.iri === chosen), returning that matching option. No branch infers or selects a different Agent; with no saved choice, eligible=false also leaves the existing null/empty/nonempty discovery branches intact.
